title: Sol–gel synthesis of ZnO@SiC heterojunctions from photovoltaic waste for enhanced paracetamol photodegradation
content:
Abstract

Exponential growth in photovoltaic energy production has created a critical environmental challenge: managing silicon carbide (SiC) waste from wafer cutting processes. This study addresses this challenge by transforming photovoltaic waste into high-value photocatalytic materials. Zinc oxide@silicon carbide (ZnO@SiC) heterojunction photocatalysts with varying SiC mass ratios (1, 3, and 7 wt%) were successfully synthesized via a sol–gel route. Comprehensive characterization confirmed the hexagonal wurtzite structure of ZnO and the formation of a heterojunction with type-II band alignment characteristics. The ZnO@SiC-3% composite exhibited exceptional photocatalytic performance, achieving complete degradation of paracetamol (PCT) (20 mg.L−1, pH = 7.5) after 180 min under UV irradiation (365 nm). This improvement is attributed to enhanced charge separation and interfacial electron transfer at the ZnO@SiC interface, supported by band gap narrowing from 3.12 to 3.04–3.08 eV. Radical scavenging experiments confirmed the dominant role of •O2 − and •OH in PCT degradation. Kinetic studies followed a pseudo-first-order model, with ZnO@SiC-3% exhibiting a rate constant of 0.0256 min−1, which is approximately twofold higher than that of pure ZnO (0.0128 min−1). The optimal catalyst dosage was 750 mg.L−1. Efficient degradation was maintained across a broad pH range (2.5–7.5). The catalyst retained 85% of its initial activity after four cycles, demonstrating good stability and reusability. The use of photovoltaic waste-derived SiC reduces the dependence on commercial SiC, highlighting the environmental and economic benefits of this sustainable approach. Overall, ZnO@SiC heterojunctions derived from photovoltaic waste offer a sustainable approach for pharmaceutical pollutant removal and photovoltaic waste valorization, supporting circular economy strategies.
